newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-MARTYN PENALTY SAVE SPARES LEEDS'S BLUSHES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MARTYN PENALTY SAVE SPARES LEEDS'S BLUSHES.

text.p: Goalkeeper Nigel Martyn saved an 88th minute penalty to prevent premier league Leeds from sliding out of the F.A. Cup at the hands of first division Crystal Palace on Tuesday.
The third round tie ended 2-2 after Martyn, the former Palace goalkeeper, dived to save Bruce Dyer's spot kick. Dyer's misery was complete when he blazed the rebound wide.

The penalty was Palace's second of the night and was as hotly disputed as the first which Dyer converted in the sixth minute to level the tie after Brian Deane had given the 1972 Cup winners an early lead.
Leeds's advantage in a frenzied opening few minutes was restored when Leif Andersen netted an own goal.
None of the four premier league sides in action in ties postponed from earlier in the month made it through to the fourth round.

Title-chasing Wimbledon had to come from behind to force a replay at second division Crewe, Aston Villa fared no better against second division opposition, drawing 0-0 with Notts County, and Derby's tie at Gillingham was abandoned midway through the second half because of a frost-bound pitch.
Three of the night's other ties between Watford and Oxford, Luton and Bolton and Brentford and Manchester City fell late victims to the frost.
Crewe's Ashley Westwood shocked 1988 Cup winners Wimbledon with a goal in the 12th minute but defender Chris Perry dragged the Dons level with a 26th minute strike.
The winners face a lucrative fourth round trip to Old Trafford to play holders Manchester United.

The tie between first division sides Queens Park Rangers and Huddersfield also appeared set for a replay until Rangers skipper Alan McDonald headed home a corner in the final minute to make it 2-1 for QPR.
Former Liverpool striker John Aldridge was sent off for foul play as first division Tranmere stumbled to a 1-0 defeat at third division Carlisle.
